# NOTES ON TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: "Ruth Fielding at Golden Pass; or, The Perils of an Artificial Avalanche" by Alice B. Emerson (Cupples & Leon, 1925; Gutenberg #76206)

### Front matter
- Series list: Ruth Fielding series (23 vols listed, incl. Red Mill, Briarwood Hall, Snow Camp, Lighthouse Point, Silver Ranch, Cliff Island, Sunrise Farm, Gypsies, Moving Pictures, Dixie, College, Saddle, Red Cross, War Front, Homeward Bound, Down East, Great Northwest, St. Lawrence, Treasure Hunting, Far North, Golden Pass); Betty Gordon series; others.
- Chapters I–XXV: Fire; Tom to the Rescue; Good Old Times; Golden Pass; A New Star; Fine News; The Leading Lady; The Party; On the Road; A Suspicious Move; Trouble in the Air; In Peril; New Worries; Helen is Hurt; Startling News; An Incredible Suggestion; Ruth Decides; A New Role; A New Friend; Not Acting; The Narrow Ledge; A Test of Courage; Buried Alive; Bears; Sunlight Once More.

### Characters
- Ruth Fielding: heroine, orphan raised by Great-uncle Jabez Potter at the Red Mill near Cheslow; scenario writer/director of Fielding Film Corporation; Red Cross trained.
- Tom Cameron: Helen's twin; Ruth's business partner; loves Ruth; jealous of Layton Boardman; rescues Ruth on ledge; saves Ruth/others in avalanche cave; shot by bear (arm).
- Helen Cameron: Ruth's chum; engaged to Chess Copley; hit by spent bullet in rodeo (scalp wound).
- Chess Copley: Helen's fiancé; uncle's money backs his business deal.
- Uncle Jabez Potter: crabbed old man. Aunt Alvirah Boggs: sweet old housekeeper, calls Ruth "my pretty."
- Jennie Marchand ("Heavy" Stone): married to Henri Marchand (Frenchman, in France). Mary Cox ("The Fox"), Ann Hicks, Nettie Parsons, Mercy Curtis (lives in Cheslow), Barclay Clayton ("Bark").
- Mr. Hammond: president of Alectrion Film Corporation; suggests Ruth act; recommends Headwaters Ranch; brings Edith Lang.
- Layton Boardman: western actor, hero; ex-Palatial Films (Sol Bloomberg quarrel); injured by horse fall (ankle, back, forehead); good with lariat/colts; says "Never cared for any girl" (reveals to Tom he was acting).
- Viola Callahan: temperamental actress hired for lead; jumped contract (note: "Tony and I are going over to Bloomberg"); with Tony Martano. Met Charlie Reid (Bloomberg's agent) in Chicago.
- Sol Bloomberg: owner of Palatial Films; sabotaging Ruth. His picture with Viola/Tony fails.
- Shepley: tall thin director, Ruth's right hand. Dave Sentner: comedian. Cameramen (two), assistant directors.
- Ma and Pa Gowdy: Headwaters Ranch owners; Andy: gangling lad; foreman (long lean blue-eyed, wrinkled smile).
- Edith Lang: crippled actress (lost leg from WWI wound/blood poisoning), coach to Ruth.
- Farstein: manager of theater.

### Events (in order)
1. Ruth's new picture "Snowblind" premieres at Palace theater, Cheslow; school chums arrive, surprise party; explosion/fire in storeroom; Tom rescues Ruth behind stage.
2. Party at hotel; Hammond arrives; Ruth announces Golden Pass, Montana for next picture "Hearts of the Mountains."
3. Ruth signs Layton Boardman (Tom objects; Tom's signature hesitates). Helen's news: uncle backs Chess's deal.
4. Viola Callahan hired at high salary; Ruth/Tom quarrel over salary.
5. Party at Red Mill; Boardman dances with girls; Tom jealous.
6. Train to Chicago; Viola suspicious meeting with Bloomberg agent Charlie Reid.
7. Arrive Headwaters Ranch; Boardman tames colt; stampede of steers; Boardman tries to save Ruth, thrown; Tom and cowboys shoot steers.
8. Helen hurt by bullet from real cartridge in rodeo (steer roping).
9. Ruth finds Viola's note: "Sorry, but Tony and I are going over to Bloomberg..."
10. Hammond proposes Ruth act; she agrees; camera tests succeed; Edith Lang arrives; coaches Ruth.
11. Tom goes to pool; bear encounter; Ruth finds him.
12. Avalanche preparation; Ruth nearly falls off ledge; Tom rescues her by jumping down, Boardman lassos them up.
13. Avalanche staged; second unplanned explosion (dynamite house) buries cast in cave; Tom finds tunnel to light; two bears in second cave; Tom shot-clawed on arm; Ruth makes tourniquet with twig; doctor praises her.
14. Chess arrives; Boardman tells Tom he never cared for girls and was acting.
15. Viola's failure; Bloomberg's scheme fails; Ruth becomes famous ("Hearts of the Mountains").
16. Final: Ruth says "So are the wicked punished!"; Helen envious: "With the world at your feet, to say nothing of Tom!"

### Key phrases
- Ruth's chum-song: "S.B.—Ah-h-h! ... Briarwood Hall! That's all!"
- "Sweetbriars, do or die."
- Hammond: "Haven't you ever thought ... what a fine actress you would make?"
- Ruth's Red Cross training; she bandages Helen.
- "One wide river to cross."

---

## BOOK 2: "The Top of the World" by Ethel M. Dell (1920; Gutenberg #12360)

Dedication: to her mother; poem "When you have reached the top of the world... by faith and love and God's goodness to my soul." Motto of the book: "By faith and love" (inscription "Fide et Amore" cut into skeleton tree by Burke).

### Parts & chapters
- PART I (Ch. I–XII): Advice; The New Mistress; The Whip-Hand; The Victory; The Miracle; The Land of Strangers; The Wrong Turning; The Comrade; The Arrival; The Dream; The Cross-Roads; The Stake.
- PART II (I–XI): Comrades; The Visitors; The Bargain; The Capture; The Good Cause; The Return; The Guest; The Interruption; The Abyss; The Desire to Live; The Remedy.
- PART III (I–XII): The New Era; Into Battle; The Seed; Mirage; Everybody's Friend; The Hero; The Net; The Summons; For the Sake of the Old Love; The Bearer of Evil Tidings; The Sharp Corner; The Cost.
- PART IV (I–XIII): Sand of the Desert; The Skeleton Tree; The Punishment; The Evil Thing; The Land of Blasted Hopes; The Parting; Piet Vreiboom; Out of the Depths; The Meeting; The Truth; The Storm; The Sacrifice; By Faith and Love.

### Characters
- Sylvia Ingleton: heroine, 23ish, tawny/red-gold hair, red-brown eyes; daughter of Squire Gilbert Ingleton of the old Manor. Mother (Mrs. Ingleton, invalid) died 3 years before. Inherits money from mother at age 25.
- Guy Ranger: her fiancé (engaged 5 years, since she was 18); son of Squire's bailiff (Ranger, yeoman); public-school educated; banished to South Africa (cousin farming). Charming, reckless, later alcoholic, morphine addict.
- Jeffcott: old head gardener, loyal to Sylvia.
- Mrs. Caroline Emmott / Mrs. Ingleton: widow, "Madam," tall, handsome, domineering, cruel; married squire; hid Guy's letters.
- George Preston: "M.F.H.", Captain Preston, rich, horsey, wants Sylvia; calls her "Cherry-ripe."
- Vernon Eversley: friendly boy.
- Bliss: butler. Mrs. Hadlow: housekeeper. Evans: postman. Winnie: Sylvia's horse (hunter) in England.
- Burke Ranger: Guy's cousin, rugged, grey eyes, Blue Hill Farm near Brennerstadt (earlier Ritzen station); "partner," calls Sylvia "little pal," "Enchantress." Shaves/chin wound plaster.
- Mary Ann: stout Kaffir/old servant ("hideous"); Joe: house boy; Fair Rosamond (Rose): Kaffir girl; Hans Schafen: Dutch overseer (rubber-soled boots).
- Piet Vreiboom: neighbour, low-browed, monkeyish, lecherous; laughs at Sylvia.
- Saul Kieff: sinister doctor, black onyx eyes, raven-like; supplies morphia; "the Devil's servant"; Burke thrashes him publicly at Brennerstadt; Kieff later kills himself with opium overdose.
- Bill Merston: red-faced jovial neighbour; wife Matilda Merston: thin, bitter, six children died; later friend to Sylvia.
- Donovan Kelly: Irish manager of diamond mine, Brennerstadt; horse St. Peter ("Pete"); "Ye"; ex-Imperial Yeomanry; helpful.
- Hoffstein: owner of bar (Hoffstein's) where Guy worked.
- Wilbraham: owns the diamond raffled (flawed, worth thousands). Guy wins it.

### Events (in order)
Part I:
- Jeffcott urges Sylvia to marry; she says only Guy. Sylvia's father remarried Mrs. Emmott (Madam) after holiday; Sylvia hates her. Sylvia's room redecorated.
- Mrs. Ingleton arrives; declares she'll dominate; "Madam" name; Preston arrives, asks Sylvia to be his wife; Mrs. Ingleton and Preston plot.
- Breakfast: Mrs. Ingleton forbids Sylvia's hunting; threatens; Sylvia says "I'll defy you."
- Hunt Ball: Preston gets her to provisionally agree to marry him if no word from Guy; she wires Guy.
- Next morning Sylvia learns from Jeffcott letters from Guy were held back (stolen by Mrs. Ingleton). Confronts; leaves home for Africa to find Guy.
- Arrive Ritzen, South Africa. Guy absent at Cape Town. Burke (not Guy) meets her; reveals Guy is in delirium/ill, drunk; "best thing to go back and marry someone else." She refuses.
- Next day Burke takes her 20 miles by cart to Blue Hill Farm; Guy's shanty at "Ritter Spruit"; Burke: "He's a rotter." She asks Burke to save Guy; Burke demands she not marry Guy.
- Dinner picnic; "comrades"; kopje (hill) with sugar-loaf shape.
- Storm: she's hurt knee; Mary Ann, Joe, Rose servants.
- Dream: two horsemen collide on ravine; she can't tell which one died.
- Piet Vreiboom visits; Burke says she is his wife; Burke proposes marriage; she agrees—married civilly (at Brennerstadt). Race to a skeleton tree; Burke carves "Fide et Amore." Burke says she's "partner"; "pals" arrangement.
Part II:
- Ride to Guy's hut (cabin on "Ritter Spruit"); Guy gone. Merstons visit; Matilda Merston bitter about husband.
- Burke: "I want to be your husband" — Sylvia asks him to help save Guy; bargain: "play a straight game."
- Burke finds Guy in Hoffstein's bar. Kelly helps. Burke fights Guy; sedates him.
- Guy taken to Burke's hut; Sylvia prepares guest-room; Guy refuses to come; Burke kisses Sylvia. Guy visits; drinks. Burke and Guy in shelter.
- Guy stays in Burke's room; Guy shoots self in doorway (boss shot) during evening; Burke keeps revolver; Kieff brought from Ritzen (doctor "Saul Kieff"); Sylvia tends Guy; Kieff gives Sylvia morphia.
Part III:
- Sylvia addicted to Kieff's injections; Burke discovers marks; Burke sends Kieff away.
- Guy recovers; Sylvia visits Merstons; Matilda's seed of friendship.
- Sylvia cuts Fair Rosamond with riding switch; Guy comforts her; says "I married him because he was so like you." Burke returns; sand-storm; Kelly arrives; Burke and Guy fight fire at Vreiboom's; Guy saves Burke from burning shed.
- Guy sleeps; Sylvia searches for lost key to strong-box.
Part IV:
- Sylvia confronts Burke; diamond; Guy steals money from strong-box; Guy wins Wilbraham diamond.
- Sylvia goes to Brennerstadt; Burke pursues; Kieff insults her; Burke thrashes Kieff publicly; Kieff dies of overdose.
- Sylvia returns to Merstons; Guy visits her at night, nearly strangles; she gives remedy; Guy dies in dawn? (Guy dies; storm; cloudburst; Burke rides to Guy's hut; hut washed away after rescue.)
- Burke goes to Guy in hut; sees Sylvia; she returns, saves Guy with Burke; Burke, Sylvia, Guy ride Diamond to safety; Guy dies (buried under kopje). Burke and Sylvia reconcile ("By faith and love"). Guy's gift: the diamond ("Tell her she is not to keep it! She is to sell it"). Burke and Sylvia plan to visit England; end: "top of the world."

### Key details
- Diamond: Burke's horse "Diamond" (black with white mark on head), Sylvia's horse. Sylvia's own horse "Winnie" in England.
- Kopje: Sylvia's favourite hill she never climbed.
- Skeleton tree: marked "Fide et Amore" (by faith and love).
- Matilda: "Happiness" recipe.
- Final line: "they were nearer to the stars above them in that moment than to the world that lay at their feet."
